issues.title: Direct import from features package
issues.description: The rule requires apps/api/v2 to import from @calcom/platform-libraries instead of directly from @calcom/features, but the code imports TeamService directly from @calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService
issues.rule_name: Prevent Circular Dependencies Between Core Packages

issues.title: Insufficient authorization - regular members can create invite links
issues.description: The endpoint uses @Roles('TEAM_MEMBER') which allows any team member to create invite links, but the business logic requires admin permissions for this sensitive operation. The e2e tests verify that only admins should be able to create invites (returning 403 for regular members), but this permission check is too permissive. This security issue allows unauthorized users to generate invite tokens that could be used to add members to teams without proper authorization.

issues.title: Inverted logic causes wrong invite URLs for organizations vs teams
issues.description: The condition `if (isOrgContext)` returns the team invite link format when it should return the organization signup format, and vice versa. Organization invites need to direct users to the signup flow with callback to getting-started, but will incorrectly receive the teams URL. Regular team invites need the teams URL but will incorrectly receive the signup URL with callback. This breaks the entire invite flow by sending users to the wrong destination based on whether they're joining an organization or a regular team.

issues.title: Wrong token value returned breaks invite link functionality
issues.description: The method returns `newToken.identifier` which contains the database identifier string 'invite-link-for-teamId-{teamId}' instead of returning the actual random hex token that was generated. This means the invite link will embed this identifier string in the URL instead of the actual verification token. When users attempt to use the invite link, the token lookup will fail because the identifier is not a valid token value, completely breaking the invite acceptance flow.

issues.title: Service filename does not match PascalCase class name
issues.description: Rule requires service filenames to match the exported class name exactly in PascalCase (e.g., TeamService.ts). This service class is `TeamService` but the file is named `teamService.ts` (camelCase), violating the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26644 - feat: api v2 team invite link endpoint
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite`, a thin controller over the shared `TeamService.createInvite`, plus the module wiring, output DTOs and an e2e spec. The endpoint itself is simple, but the diff also changes the shared service in two ways that break the invite flow. `TeamService.createInvite` now returns `newToken.identifier` (a constant string like `invite-link-for-teamId-5`) as `token` instead of the random token. `buildInviteLink` has its condition flipped, so regular teams get the signup/getting-started link and org teams get `/teams`. Because `TeamService` is shared, the tRPC `teams.createInvite` path used by the web invite modal is affected as well.

The controller also has `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")` where the PR description and the spec require `TEAM_ADMIN`, so any team member can mint invite links. The e2e tests as written would fail on three assertions: the member 403 test, the new-token-per-request test, and the token-in-link checks. The PR checklist's "verify E2E tests pass" item is not satisfied. This needs changes before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Three defects are each independently merge-blocking. The role is too permissive (`TEAM_MEMBER` passes the guard for every membership, so the required 403 for non-admin members will not happen). The returned `token` is the wrong value and is not the token embedded in the link. The link-type condition is inverted, which also changes behavior for the existing web invite flow. The spec's own tests would catch the first and second defects, which shows the suite was not run green on this head.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, team invite links are generated only by `TeamService.createInvite` in `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts`. It is called from the tRPC `teams.createInvite` handler (used by `MemberInvitationModal.tsx`) and from the existing org-scoped controller `OrganizationsTeamsInviteController`. Each call writes a `verificationToken` row with identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` and a 7-day expiry, then builds a URL. API v2 requests pass through `ApiAuthGuard` and `RolesGuard`. `RolesGuard` reads `@Roles` metadata and compares it against the caller's team membership role using the `TEAM_ROLES` ordering (OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER).

This PR adds `TeamsInviteModule` and `TeamsInviteController` under `/v2/teams/:teamId`, and registers the module in `platform-endpoints-module.ts`. The controller delegates to the shared service and wraps the result in `{ status, data }`. It also changes the shared service: the created token value is now taken from the DB row's identifier, and the `isOrgContext` branch in `buildInviteLink` is flipped. Both changes apply to every caller of `TeamService.createInvite`, not only the new endpoint.
steps: Entry point: an authenticated HTTP POST hits `TeamsInviteController.createInvite` at `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite`. `ApiAuthGuard` resolves the user and `RolesGuard` checks the `@Roles` value. The PR sets this to `TEAM_MEMBER`, so the gate is wider than the spec's TEAM_ADMIN.
The controller calls `TeamService.createInvite(teamId)`. For a new invite, the service generates a random 32-byte hex token and inserts a `verificationToken` row with a 7-day expiry.

The PR changes the return value to `token: newToken.identifier`. That is the constant identifier string, not the random token. The `inviteLink` is still built from the raw random token, so the returned `token` does not match the link.

`buildInviteLink` now returns the `/teams?token=` link when `isOrgContext` is true and the `/signup?...&callbackUrl=` link otherwise. This is the reverse of the PR description and of the original code. The existing-token path in the same service also uses this helper, so the web tRPC flow is affected too.

The controller wraps the result as `{ status: SUCCESS_STATUS, data }` using `CreateInviteOutputDto`. This matches the existing org controller's response shape, though the DTO file is duplicated rather than shared.

findings.title: Endpoint is gated to TEAM_MEMBER, so any team member can create invite links
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.ts`, the `createInvite` handler at line 32 is decorated with `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`. Change it to `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")` so that only team admins and owners can create invite links, as the PR description and spec require. Keep the rest of the decorator stack unchanged. Then run `teams-invite.controller.e2e-spec.ts` and confirm that the "non-admin member" test (around line 148) receives 403.

findings.title: Returned `token` is the DB identifier, not the random token embedded in the link
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts`, `TeamService.createInvite` (around lines 88-101) now returns `token: newToken.identifier`. The identifier is the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`, not the random token that is embedded in `inviteLink`. Return the locally generated `token` variable instead, which is also what the existing-token branch returns (`existingToken.token`). Drop the `const newToken =` assignment if it is no longer needed. Verify that `teams-invite.controller.e2e-spec.ts` ("should create a new invite on each request" and the `toContain(token)` assertions) passes.

findings.title: `buildInviteLink` condition is inverted, so regular and org teams get each other's links
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/ee/teams/services/teamService.ts`, `TeamService.buildInviteLink` (around line 104-111) has its condition flipped from `if (!isOrgContext)` to `if (isOrgContext)`. Restore the original negation so that regular teams (non-org, non-org-sub-team) return the `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=` link, and org or org-sub-team contexts return the `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=<getting-started path>` link. Check that the existing-token and new-token paths both use this helper and that the web invite modal in `apps/web/modules/ee/teams/components/MemberInvitationModal.tsx` still gets the same link format it had before this PR.

findings.title: Tests don't cover invite link routing for org and regular teams
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.e2e-spec.ts`, add coverage for the invite link shape. Add one test where a regular team (`isOrganization: false`, no parent) gets an `inviteLink` that starts with `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=`. Add a second test for an org or org-sub-team that gets a `/signup?token=` link containing `callbackUrl=`. Use exact prefix assertions rather than `toContain(token)` alone, so a future flip in `TeamService.buildInviteLink` fails the test. Follow the setup pattern already used in the file.

findings.title: Import from `@calcom/features` breaks the API v2 convention of using `@calcom/platform-libraries`
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.ts` (line 21), `TeamService` is imported from `@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService`. Change this to `@calcom/platform-libraries`, matching `apps/api/v2/src/modules/organizations/teams/invite/controllers/organizations-teams-invite.controller.ts`. Then remove the duplicate `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/outputs/invite.output.ts` and import `CreateInviteOutputDto` from `@/modules/organizations/teams/invite/outputs/invite.output` (or move the DTO to a shared module). Confirm the API still builds and the e2e spec runs.

findings.title: No rate limit or cap on invite token creation
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/invite/controllers/teams-invite.controller.ts`, the `createInvite` handler (around lines 30-38) creates a new 7-day invite token on every call. Decide whether to reuse a still-valid invite token for the team or to add a per-team or per-key throttle. If you reuse tokens, look up the existing `verificationToken` rows with identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` and `expires >= now` in `TeamService.createInvite`. Track this as a follow-up and keep it out of this PR if the team agrees.

findings.title: Module wiring and controller structure follow the existing v2 pattern
findings.body: `TeamsInviteModule` is registered in `platform-endpoints-module.ts` beside `TeamsMembershipsModule`, and the controller uses the same `ApiAuthGuard, RolesGuard` stack and `/v2/teams/:teamId/*` path shape as the sibling controllers. The e2e spec uses the same `withApiAuth` harness and `supertest` default import as the rest of the v2 suite, and it includes a non-member case in addition to the member case.
